new_page.title: BC Home Owner Grant 2026: $2,075,000 Threshold & How to Claim
new_page.h1: What is the BC home owner grant threshold for 2026?
new_page.description: The 2026 BC home owner grant threshold is $2,075,000. Above it the grant falls by $5 for every $1,000 of value. You must apply every year.

breadcrumbs.name: What is the BC home owner grant threshold for 2026?

faq.q: Do I get the home owner grant automatically?
faq.a: No. You apply each year, even if nothing changed.

faq.q: Does a rental property get the grant?
faq.a: No. The grant is for the home you live in as your principal residence.

parts.t: $2,075,000. If your home is assessed at or below that, you can claim the full grant on your 2026 property taxes. Above it, the grant drops by $5 for every $1,000 of extra value until it reaches zero. You must apply every year, and pay at least $350 in property tax.

From January 1, 2027 the regular grant is $570. Seniors 65 and over, veterans and people with disabilities can get a larger, additional grant. The Province lists the current amounts on its home owner grant page.
The regular grant reaches $0 at an assessed value of $2,189,000. The additional grant reaches $0 at $2,244,000.
Online through the Province, each year after your property tax notice arrives. The home has to be your principal residence.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
